findings.title: Crash when booking a Google Meet event with no destination calendar
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` gives `undefined` whenever the event has no destination calendar. `handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1067` now sets `destinationCalendar: null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has one. The next line reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` with no optional chaining. So when `evt.location === MeetLocationType`, this throws a TypeError and the booking fails, when it should fall back to Cal Video. The old code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`. Fix: use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

findings.title: Video booking references no longer store their credentialId
findings.body: The old code was `credentialId: isCalendarType ? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId : result.credentialId`, so video references (for example a Zoom or Daily result from `createVideoEvent`) kept `result.credentialId`. The new code is `isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`, which drops the credentialId for every non-calendar reference. Later updates or deletes that find the video credential through `reference.credentialId` can no longer link the meeting to its credential. Fix: keep `result.credentialId` in both branches, since `createEvent` now fills it for calendars as well.

findings.title: Fallback calendar lookup in updateEvent/deleteEvent can never match
findings.body: This fallback only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, and it then searches for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId`, i.e. a calendar whose externalId is null or undefined. In practice it always returns `undefined`. Before this change it fell back to the destination calendar's externalId. Now, for references saved without `externalCalendarId` (older bookings), `events.update` is called with `calendarId: undefined` (line 261), and `deleteEvent` (line 317) quietly switches to `primary`. An event stored on a non-primary calendar is then not updated, or not deleted (the 404 is resolved silently at line 335). Fix: fall back to the destination calendar that matches this service's credential, or to `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId`.

findings.title: Org slug condition is inverted
findings.body: The old code was `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`: the slug was set directly only when team billing is disabled, and with billing enabled it went into `metadata.requestedSlug` until payment. The rewrite `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` reverses this. With billing enabled, the org gets its slug immediately, before payment, and also carries `requestedSlug`. Self-hosted instances without billing create orgs with no slug at all. Fix: `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. Line 153 is correct as it stands.

findings.title: Team members' non-Google calendars are written to the host's calendar id
findings.body: For collective events, `createAllCalendarEvents` (EventManager.ts:339-370) now calls `createEvent` once per destination, each time with that member's credential. Google looks up its calendar by `credentialId`, but Office365 (this line), Lark (larkcalendar CalendarService.ts:128) and CalDAV (packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156) always take `destinationCalendar[0]`, the main host's calendar. A member's Office365 credential then posts to `/me/calendars/<host's id>/events`, which fails, and CalDAV filters to a URL the member doesn't have, so nothing is created. Either way the event never appears on the member's calendar, and nothing tells them. Fix: pass `credentialId` and match on it, as Google does. Alternatively, `createEvent` in CalendarManager could pass `externalId` through.

findings.title: Collective members' calendars are dropped when the organizer has no destination calendar
findings.body: When neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` is set, `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` (line 1067). In that case `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` does nothing, and the destination calendars of the other collective hosts are silently thrown away. Fix: initialise the array as `[]` (or build it as `[...main, ...teamDestinationCalendars]`). Keep in mind that `createAllCalendarEvents` treats a non-empty array differently from the no-destination fallback.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation repeats all deletes once per calendar reference
findings.body: This recurring branch now sits inside `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`. For each reference it deletes every remaining occurrence with all of the organizer's calendar credentials, and it ignores which credential the reference belongs to. A booking with N calendar references therefore issues N copies of the same deletes, and other team members' recurring events are never deleted. Consider running this branch once, outside the loop, and deleting per reference credential.

findings.title: Dynamic users no longer select `organization`, and error status codes changed
findings.body: The rewritten `loadUsers` drops `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the dynamic-user query, but `IsFixedAwareUser` (line 355) still declares `organization: { slug: string }`, so code that reads `user.organization` on dynamic bookings now gets undefined. Separately, the plain `Error` thrown for an empty `dynamicUserList` (line 728) does not match the `HttpError`/Prisma checks, so it comes back as a 500 "Unable to load users" instead of an empty list leading to the existing not-found handling. Also, `eventType.users` (line 755) lost its `|| []` fallback. Please restore the `organization` select and return a 4xx for the bad-input case.

summary:
This PR turns `destinationCalendar` into an array so collective events can be written to each member's calendar. I read all 22 files; this was a read-only review, so nothing was built or run. I found two blockers and five fixes:

**Blockers**
- **Meet bookings crash:** in `EventManager.create`, a Google Meet booking crashes with a TypeError when the organizer has no destination calendar, because `.integration` is read on an undefined element. It should fall back to Cal Video instead.
- **Org slug logic inverted:** in `organizations/create.handler.ts`, the condition for setting the org slug is reversed. With billing on, the slug is set before payment; with billing off, orgs get no slug.

**Fixes**
- **Video references lose their credentialId:** video meetings can no longer be linked to their credential for later updates or deletes.
- **Google update/delete fallback never matches:** for older bookings saved without a calendar id, events on a non-primary calendar are not updated or not deleted.
- **Office365/Lark/CalDAV use the host's calendar:** they always write to the first (host's) calendar, so collective members on those providers silently get no event.
- **Members' calendars dropped:** when the organizer has no destination calendar, the other collective members' calendars are thrown away.
- **`loadUsers` regressions:** dynamic users no longer select `organization`, an empty dynamic user list now returns a 500, and the `|| []` fallback on `eventType.users` is gone.

I also flagged, as "consider", that cancelling a recurring booking repeats all deletes once per calendar reference.
